title: Alternate Path Fetch
problem: Scaling pipeline width is challenging due to limitations on instruction renaming and branch prediction per cycle, and branch mispredictions reduce useful fetch bandwidth. Modern out-of-order cores face a difficult tradeoff between wider monolithic pipelines and practical implementation constraints.
motivation: Improving frontend utilization and reducing pipeline refill delays from branch mispredictions is critical for maximizing performance in wide out-of-order cores.
method: APF uses a Parallel Fetch scheme to split the processor pipeline into two parallel sections that run simultaneously. One section handles regular instructions normally, while the second speculatively (tentatively) processes hard-to-predict branches by predicting their direction and pre-processing the fetch, decode, and partial rename steps for the instructions that might follow. This approach lets the processor efficiently use wide frontend bandwidth without the engineering complexity of a single monolithic (extremely wide) pipeline.
key_novelty: The core insight is using partial renaming—tracking only critical register mappings—on speculative alternate paths rather than fully renaming all speculatively-executed instructions, delivering better performance with lower hardware complexity.
contributions: Dual-pipeline architecture dividing regular and speculative alternate-path instruction processing
Parallel Fetch scheme enabling simultaneous operation of two independent pipelines without front-end overhead
Demonstration that partial renaming on alternate paths is superior to full execution on both sides of branches
5% geomean speedup over aggressive 8-wide out-of-order core with improved frontend utilization
primary_theme: speculative branch prediction with parallel pipelines
